and what was spoken for you
the app asks YES / NO / WAIT; sign or tap

• A hand left the frame for > 0.3 s:
[?] with "keep both hands in the frame"
• Signed YES / NO / WAIT while the agent
is asking you: it answers the question
rehearsed: hello, thank you, yes, no,
• Sign Lab: local backend with a
• Nothing is spoken unless you tapped SEND (live call) or
• Unsure recognition stays silent: [?] or "did you mean", never a guess.
• The agent never agrees to anything outside the brief: it asks
you, or says it will call back.
• The draft may reword your signs but never adds a day, time,
• Calls go only to allowlisted, consenting numbers, from
Ishara's number, and say they are for a Deaf caller.
• Built and tested in the iOS simulator: both call modes, and the
ASL model running inside the app.
• App vs Mac on the same 18 ASL test clips: same decision on 17;
the same chip on all 9 the Mac was sure of.
• End to end against our real backend code with a scripted
• Not yet: phone-camera clips, iPhone speed, a real Bolna call.
• No Deaf user has tested it. ISL is the goal; it is blocked by data.
Ishara: sign what you need, approve it, and the call is made for you
Architecture as of 27 October 2026 (decisions D1, D8, D9 in PLAN.md). Blue runs on the iPhone, yellow on our backend, purple at Bolna, green is the user's own action.
1. Live call: you sign each reply; it is spoken only after you tap SEND
Bonus (Path A): your own Phone call with Apple's Add Audio in Calls plays the approved sentence; no captions in the app.
2. Call for me: you approve a brief once; the agent makes the call and brings back notes
3. How a sign becomes a chip (on the phone, nothing uploaded)
5. Rules that never bend, and where the build is
